sections.h2: Where do I deal with property tax in Osceola County?
sections.html:
Osceola County splits the job across the Property Appraiser, the Tax Collector and the Clerk of the Circuit Court and County Comptroller. Each has a separate phone line and a separate part of the process, so match your question to the right door.

The Property Appraiser sets assessed value and handles exemptions, tangible property returns and the tax roll. Its main number is (407) 742-5000, and its site has a tax estimator and a homestead filing page. The Tax Collector prints and mails tax notices, takes payment and runs the tax certificate process. The clerk, acting as county recorder, keeps the Official Records where deeds and mortgages are filed.

The Tax Collector lists four offices, all open Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm at 407-742-4000: the main office at 2501 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy in Kissimmee, one at 2595 Simpson Road in Kissimmee, a St. Cloud office at 1300 9th Street, Suite 101B, and a Campbell City office at 4730 South Orange Blossom Trail. Appointments can be booked online.

  • Osceola County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, millage page, tax estimator.
  • Osceola County Tax Collector: notices, payment, installment plan, certificates.
  • Osceola Clerk of the Circuit Court and County Comptroller: Official Records search, which includes a property fraud alert signup.

sections.h2: What are the Osceola County property tax dates?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector's calendar runs November through March for payment, with April 1 as the delinquency date. Collection begins on November 1 for the January through December year, and notices normally mail on or before that day to the address on the tax roll.

Owners who pay through an escrow account should know the mortgage company is supposed to request the bill, and the owner receives a copy. The collector reminds taxpayers that it is the owner's responsibility to make sure the tax is paid and a bill is received.

The Property Appraiser's important dates page lists January 1 as the assessment and valuation date, March 1 as the exemption filing deadline and April 1 for tangible personal property returns. The office also posts its closure days, including Veterans Day, the Thanksgiving days, Christmas Eve and Day and New Year's Day.

sections.h2: What early payment discounts and installment options does Osceola County offer?
sections.html:
Paying early cuts the bill by a set percentage that declines each month. The Tax Collector prints it as 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January, 1 percent in February, and the gross amount in March.

The installment plan splits the bill into four payments, and its calendar shows the traps. The application is due April 30. The first payment is due on or before June 30. If it arrives in July, the discount is gone and a 5 percent penalty is added, and a first payment that does not reach the office by July 31 cancels participation. The second payment is due September 30 and the third December 31.

Tangible personal property tax is a separate bill on furniture, fixtures and equipment in businesses and in rental property, plus structural additions to mobile homes. If the estimated tax is above $100.00 it may be paid quarterly. A landlord who sells a furnished rental should ask the appraiser about the return due April 1.

  • Discounts apply to both real estate and tangible personal property bills.
  • Changes to name, address or assessed value go through the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector.

sections.h2: How does homestead work for an Osceola County seller or buyer?
sections.html:
The Property Appraiser's FAQ and dates page set March 1 as the filing deadline, and the benefit starts for the year you file in. State materials describe a homestead exemption of up to $50,000, built from a first $25,000 that covers school taxes and an added amount for non-school taxes on value above $50,000.

The appraiser's site has a File Homestead page and a form for reporting exemption fraud, and the clerk offers a property fraud alert. If you sell, tell the appraiser; a sale or deed is a change of ownership that ends the capped assessment and resets value on the next January 1. A buyer who will live in the house must file new, by March 1.

Agricultural land is a separate classification. Osceola's appraiser notes that it does not transfer with a sale, so a buyer of a grove or pasture parcel must file again between January 1 and March 1, and that the office re-inspects classified land at least once every three years.

sections.h2: What happens if Osceola County property tax goes delinquent?
sections.html:
On April 1 the unpaid tax gets a 3 percent charge, then the parcel is advertised, then a lien is sold, and after two years the certificate holder may apply for a tax deed. The Tax Collector's pages lay out the sequence.

The delinquent list runs in a local newspaper once a week for three consecutive weeks before the sale, in parcel order. On or before June 1, the Tax Collector holds a public online sale through LienHub. Bidding opens at 18 percent and the certificate goes to the investor who accepts the lowest rate. The certificate is a lien, not a deed, and it gives the buyer no right to enter the property.

To clear it, you pay the certificate amount plus interest at the rate it sold for, and a $6.25 redemption fee on or after June 1. County held certificates, those no investor bought, are sold later through LienHub. If a certificate is not redeemed by April 1 two years after the sale, the holder may apply for a tax deed and must pay off any other certificates and the current year's tax.

  • A certificate holder may not contact you to demand payment until two years after April 1 of the issue year.
  • You can sell with a lien in place; the title company pays it from proceeds.

sections.h2: What does selling a house in Osceola County involve for the tax and the deed?
sections.html:
Closing clears the tax lien and the clerk records the deed in the Official Records. Florida's documentary stamp tax on the deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county but Miami-Dade, and all parties to the document are liable for it.

Recording fees under state law start at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus a modernization trust fund charge and a technology charge per page. The clerk collects the stamp tax at recording. Osceola's clerk also operates branch offices, including a Poinciana location, so recording does not require a trip to the courthouse in Kissimmee.

Tax cycles matter at the table. Bills mail in November, and a closing before then leaves the new year's bill unissued. Ask the title company how it will prorate, and keep the Tax Collector's payoff letter in your closing file. If the 10 percent non-homestead cap applied to your rental, expect the buyer's value to reset after the sale.

faqs.q: When does Osceola County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1. The Tax Collector adds a 3 percent charge to the gross amount that day, advertises the delinquent list, and holds an online tax certificate sale on or before June 1.

faqs.q: What discounts does the Osceola County Tax Collector give?
faqs.a: It prints 4 percent for November, 3 percent for December, 2 percent for January and 1 percent for February. Payment in March carries no discount, and March 31 is the gross due date.

faqs.q: Where is the Osceola County Tax Collector?
faqs.a: The main office is at 2501 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy in Kissimmee, with other offices on Simpson Road in Kissimmee, in St. Cloud and in Campbell City. The phone is 407-742-4000, open Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:00 pm.

faqs.q: How do I redeem an Osceola County tax certificate?
faqs.a: Pay the certificate amount plus interest at the rate it sold for, and a $6.25 fee when redeeming on or after June 1. Contact the Tax Collector for the exact payoff.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Osceola County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays with the parcel and the title company pays it from your proceeds at closing. Request a payoff figure from the Tax Collector at 407-742-4000 before you sign.
